Section 3 rejects it as an IDIQ umbrella: this is a multiple-award, five-year-ordering-period IDIQ for rapid prototype development, hardware fabrication and prototype pre-production units spanning battle management systems, AAV projects, manned and unmanned platform integration, robotic systems and weapon control systems. AAV is one of five listed technology areas in a ceiling with no task orders awarded, so no dollar of this action is identifiable to the Amphibious Assault Vehicle PE's own work.

proposals.announcement_evidence: in support of the battle management systems, assault amphibious vehicle projects, manned and unmanned platform integration and robotic systems, and weapon control systems development
proposals.rationale: The sibling award in the same daily digest paragraph set and on the same solicitation as record 18, to a second awardee under the same multiple-award IDIQ, with the name spelled here exactly as the index row has it ('assault amphibious vehicle projects'). Rejected for the same section 3 reason: a shared IDIQ ceiling listing AAV as one of five technology areas, with funding obligated only on future task orders, attributes nothing to the Amphibious Assault Vehicle PE.

proposals.announcement_evidence: sustainment efforts and operations and maintenance services in support of Low Rate Initial Production Lot VIII F135 propulsion systems
proposals.rationale: The only F135 row in this org's index is the Engine Core Upgrade under 0604840N (F-35 C2D2), and the announcement names neither ECU nor any upgrade - it names LRIP Lot VIII propulsion system sustainment, repair of repairables and replenishment spares, on a December 2014 award that predates ECU entirely. The money confirms the mismatch: fiscal 2015 operations and maintenance funds, i.e. O&M sustainment proposed against an RDT&E development line. Rejected on both identity and money colour.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Hornet Extension Project upgrades for the government of Canada
proposals.rationale: The only token shared with the index is 'Hornet', which section 3 treats as a weak generic name when it stands alone. The subject is the CF-18, Canada's legacy Hornet fleet, and the award builds the CF-18 Advanced Distributed Combat Training System Phase Three under the Hornet Extension Project - a different aircraft from the US F/A-18E/F that BLI 0145 funds. Every dollar is Foreign Military Sales customer funds ($47,114,018), so nothing here executes a US aircraft procurement line.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Littoral Combat Ship Mission Module engineering and sustainment support
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the LCS Mission Module program, so this is a real candidate rather than a coincidence, but the funded content is the section 3 generic-services pattern in its plainest form: 'engineering and sustainment support', paid with fiscal 2023 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds. O&M sustainment proposed against 0603596N, an RDT&E line whose narrative content is the MCM, SUW and MPCE development packages, is precisely the appropriation mismatch lens A exists to catch. The OPN alternatives 1600 and 1601 fail the same way - O&M is neither RDT&E nor procurement.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Littoral Combat Ship Mission Module engineering and sustainment support
proposals.rationale: The same modification to N00024-17-C-6311 re-announced four days later in a different article, carried on its own record index as the rubric requires. Rejected for the same reason as record 44: LCS Mission Module engineering and sustainment support is generic sustainment services under section 3, funded with fiscal 2023 O&M (Navy), which cannot execute the RDT&E Mission Modules line.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the construction of facilities to support the cultural and process improvement program MQ-9 Mission Control Element Group at Shaw Air Force Base, South Carolina
proposals.rationale: The MQ-9 designator is present, which is why this is recorded rather than dropped, but section 3 rejects construction outright: the award builds a headquarters building and an operations building with an exterior courtyard, competitively procured by NAVFAC and announced under the Navy. The index row MQ-9A belongs to BLI 0452, Marine Group 5 UAS - the Marine Corps aircraft procurement line - whereas these facilities house Air Force remotely piloted aircraft missions at Shaw AFB. Neither the work nor the owning service matches the line.

proposals.program_name: F-18E/F and EA-18G Modernization and Sustainment
proposals.announcement_evidence: integrated logistics support and sustaining engineering for F/A-18A-D, F/A-18E/F, and EA-18G aircraft
proposals.lexicon_quote: F-18E/F and EA-18G Modernization and Sustainment
proposals.rationale: The announcement's aircraft list overlaps the index name almost word for word, making this the most confusable record in the chunk. Section 3 still rejects it: the scope is integrated logistics support and sustaining engineering - logistics, provisioning, information systems, technical data updates, support equipment engineering and training - which is generic services, and it spans three aircraft types across the US Navy plus seven FMS governments (Australia, Canada, Spain, Finland, Switzerland, Kuwait, Malaysia), so no part of the action is identifiable to the single modernization and sustainment line's own work. The named aircraft are platforms the task order supports, not the funded program.
